strengths: The paper addresses a highly practical and often overlooked problem in causal discovery: the presence of skewed noise in location-scale noise models (LSNMs).
The proposed SKEWD method extends LSNMs to skew-normal noise distributions, significantly widening the applicability of such models to asymmetric real-world data.

The optimization framework is well-designed, successfully combining CMA-ES with an Expectation Conditional Maximization (ECM) algorithm to handle the challenging, non-convex optimization of the penalized log-likelihood.
The paper provides extensive experiments on both newly generated skewed noise datasets and 13 established benchmarks, showcasing strong and robust performance.
The appendix is rich with technical details, including the full mathematical derivations of the E-step and CM-steps of the ECM algorithm, which aids reproducibility.
weaknesses: The parameter estimation pipeline is computationally demanding, as it involves Bayesian optimization for hyperparameter tuning, CMA-ES for stochastic global search, and ECM for local refinement. This might limit its practical efficiency.

For the likelihood-scoring variant (SKEWD-LL), the assumption that the marginals are Gaussian (and thus can be neglected) is a strong assumption that may be violated in practice when the underlying causal mechanisms are highly non-linear and noise is heavily skewed.
The paper is strictly limited to the bivariate case, and extending the proposed optimization framework to multivariate causal discovery could be computationally prohibitive.

strengths: Addresses an important and realistic limitation in causal discovery: the assumption of symmetric noise (like Gaussian or Student-t) in Location-Scale Noise Models (LSNMs), which is frequently violated by skewed real-world data.
Proposes a mathematically rigorous framework (SKEWD) that models noise using a skew-normal distribution while representing the location and scale functions via penalized cubic B-splines.

Devises a solid parameter estimation procedure combining Bayesian optimization, CMA-ES, and an Expectation Conditional Maximization (ECM) algorithm to handle the challenging, non-convex optimization landscape of skew-normal likelihoods.

Provides a thorough empirical evaluation on both newly created skewed noise datasets (using both skew-normal and generalized normal distributions) and 13 established benchmark datasets, showing highly competitive performance.
weaknesses: High computational complexity: The optimization pipeline is multi-layered, involving Bayesian optimization with cross-validation, CMA-ES for initial estimation, and an ECM algorithm where one of the conditional maximization steps itself requires CMA-ES due to the lack of an analytical solution. A comprehensive discussion or benchmark of the execution runtime is missing.

The likelihood scoring variant (SKEWD-LL) assumes the marginal distributions of the variables are normal to neglect marginal log-likelihoods. If the causal variable itself is highly non-Gaussian or skewed, this assumption is violated, which could degrade performance.
The method is strictly limited to bivariate causal discovery, and extending it to multivariate networks is left as future work, limiting its immediate applicability to larger causal systems.

strengths: Addresses an important and highly practical limitation of current Location-Scale Noise Models (LSNMs) by relaxing the symmetric/normal noise assumption to handle skewed noise.
Formulates a mathematically rigorous framework utilizing skew-normal distributions combined with flexible natural cubic B-splines.
Presents a comprehensive evaluation against a wide range of state-of-the-art baselines on both custom skewed-noise datasets and multiple established benchmarks.
weaknesses: The assumption that marginal distributions p(X) and p(Y) can be modeled as standard normal after standardization is mathematically incorrect. Standardization only matches the first two moments (mean and variance) and does not transform a skewed or multi-modal distribution into a normal one. Because the paper specifically targets skewed data, assuming normal marginals for the likelihood-based scoring is highly contradictory and limits the reliability of SKEWD-LL on real-world data.

The optimization pipeline is exceedingly complex and computationally expensive. Running Bayesian Optimization (with k-fold cross-validation), CMA-ES (with population size 100 and up to 5000 iterations), and a subsequent ECM algorithm (up to 5000 iterations) in both causal directions makes the algorithm scale poorly and impractical for graphs with more than two variables. A runtime comparison with baselines is missing.

The practical utility of the proposed method on real-world data is not fully demonstrated. On the 13 established benchmarks (Table 1), SKEWD-IT (85.02%) and SKEWD-LL (77.43%) are outperformed by the baseline ROCHE (87.69%), which suggests that the massive computational overhead of SKEWD does not yield a clear benefit over simpler robust baselines outside of highly specific synthetic skewed LSNMs.

The methodological novelty in the optimization section is somewhat incremental, as it largely adapts an existing ECM algorithm for heteroscedastic partially linear models (Ferreira et al., 2023) and wraps it with standard heuristic optimizers (CMA-ES, Bayesian Optimization).

strengths: The paper addresses a highly practical and common issue in causal discovery: the assumption of symmetric noise distributions in location-scale noise models (LSNMs). It demonstrates that SOTA methods degrade when noise is skewed and offers a robust solution.

SKEWD is technically sound, successfully integrating generalized additive models (GAMs) with skew-normal distributions and utilizing a robust parameter estimation pipeline that combines Bayesian Optimization, CMA-ES, and an ECM algorithm.
The framework provides both independence-testing (SKEWD-IT) and likelihood-scoring (SKEWD-LL) variants, which are extended to the multivariate setting (SKEWD-MV) utilizing Markov equivalence classes.

Extensive empirical evaluation is performed on both novel skewed-noise datasets and 13 established benchmarks, showing that SKEWD is highly robust under skewed conditions and performs competitively on standard benchmarks.

The paper and appendix are exceptionally well-written and structured, with thorough details on proofs, implementation, hyperparameter choices, and comprehensive ablation studies (such as evaluating the impact of the ECM refinement and marginal density estimation via KDE).
weaknesses: Scalability is a notable limitation for the multivariate extension (SKEWD-MV), as fitting the skew-normal LSNM is computationally intensive. The number of parent-child configurations can grow exponentially with undirected edges, making the method less suitable for larger or denser graphs.

SKEWD's optimization pipeline is complex, relying on sequential steps of Bayesian optimization, CMA-ES, and ECM. This multi-stage process could make the method sensitive to local optima and increases the implementation overhead.

SKEWD-LL assumes Gaussian marginal distributions to neglect marginal log-likelihoods in bivariate cases. Although the authors explore nonparametric KDE in the appendix, its performance is sometimes lower than the parametric version, highlighting some sensitivity to marginal distribution misspecification.

strengths: Addresses an important and common limitation of current location-scale noise models (LSNMs), namely the assumption of symmetric/Gaussian noise, which is frequently violated in real-world applications.

The proposed method, SKEWD, is technically sound and combines generalized additive models (GAMs) using B-splines with a robust optimization pipeline consisting of Bayesian Optimization, CMA-ES, and an Expectation Conditional Maximization (ECM) algorithm.

Thorough experimental evaluation on both newly proposed benchmarks with varying degrees of skewness (under both skew-normal and generalized normal noise) and 13 established benchmarks, showing that SKEWD is highly robust under skewed noise while remaining competitive under symmetric settings.

Very clear writing, helpful illustrative figures (such as Figures 1 & 3 depicting residual dependencies), and a comprehensive appendix that includes proofs, implementation details, and insightful ablation studies.
weaknesses: High computational complexity: The optimization pipeline (BO + CMA-ES + ECM) is heavy. Running CMA-ES with a population size of 100 for up to 5000 iterations, coupled with cross-validation for hyperparameter tuning, makes SKEWD computationally demanding. A quantitative runtime analysis comparing SKEWD with other baselines (e.g., LOCI, ROCHE) is missing.

Sensitivity to marginal distribution assumptions: SKEWD-LL and SKEWD-MV rely on the assumption of Gaussian marginals to neglect the marginal log-likelihoods during scoring. If the marginals are highly non-Gaussian, this assumption can degrade performance. Although the authors present an ablation study using Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) in the appendix, the results show that KDE marginal estimation is often less stable and can decrease accuracy when the Gaussian assumption is approximately met.

strengths: Addresses an important and realistic limitation of existing location-scale noise models (LSNMs)—specifically, the common assumption of symmetric noise distributions, which fails in many real-world datasets.

The proposed method, SKEWD, is technically sound, adapting a rigorous expectation conditional maximization (ECM) framework combined with generalized additive models (GAMs) and spline smoothing to model skew-normal noise.
Provides both bivariate cause-effect inference strategies (likelihood-scoring and independence-testing) and a well-reasoned multivariate extension (SKEWD-MV) over Markov Equivalence Classes.
Features an extensive empirical evaluation, comparing SKEWD against a wide range of state-of-the-art baselines on both newly designed skewed-noise datasets and 13 established benchmark suites.

The authors include rigorous ablation studies (e.g., evaluating the necessity of the ECM step over CMA-ES alone, and examining kernel density estimation for marginals) which adds to the transparency and completeness of the work.
weaknesses: The parameter estimation pipeline is highly complex and heuristic-dependent, requiring a sequential process of Bayesian optimization, CMA-ES initialization, and ECM refinement. This multi-stage process could be prone to local optima or convergence issues on challenging real-world data.

High computational cost and limited scalability: fitting skew-normal LSNMs with splines in the multivariate setting scales exponentially with the number of unoriented edges in the MEC, making the method impractical for large or dense graphs.

On standard, non-skewed benchmarks (Table 1), SKEWD does not consistently outperform existing baselines like ROCHE or LOCI, indicating that the added complexity and computational overhead might only be justified when high skewness is explicitly expected.

The likelihood-scoring variant (SKEWD-LL) relies on the strong assumption of Gaussian marginal distributions to neglect marginal log-likelihoods. When this assumption is violated, the method suffers, and using KDE to estimate marginals introduces high variance and degrades performance in several experiments.
